items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Nevins and I were raised up in the same neighborhood... we all went to grade school... Nevins and I used to run over to the South Side Boys Club

ctx.x: He said that you inspired him rather late?

I inspired him when Reverend Turner (PHONETIC) made that first old fiddle for me. Nevins and I were raised up in the same neighborhood, you know, on the South Side, at [unintelligible] and Ricards (PHONETIC), the trumpet player and Tommy "Madman" Jones (PHONETIC), Dinah Washington, who was Ruth Jones, when we knew her -- we all went to grade school -- went to Dolittle. Eddie Chamblee Shamanie (PHONETIC), tenor player -- we all was raised in the same neighborhood somewhere and Nevins and I used to run over to the…

He saw me one summer day after Reverend Turner made that fiddle, he was coming through the alley and I'm on the back porch playing with it and he said, "Let me play it." I said, "You think you can play it?" He said, "Yeah." He grabbed it and naturally he didn't know nothing about it. He was a beautiful person. So I took it from him.
